os-efcore-mysql.title: MySQL
os-efcore-mysql.summary: MySQL with a safe setup: SSL required, utf8mb4 for every language, the provider's own retries, dates in UTC with microseconds, and its error numbers turned into clear results. Your code never names the provider underneath.

gives.1: SSL is required, utf8mb4 is used and the client never fetches the server's public key, whatever the connection string says.
gives.2: Dates are stored as UTC `datetime(6)`, so fractional seconds are kept.
gives.3: The API is ours, so the provider underneath can change later without touching your code.

connection.title: Connecting safely
connection.summary: Give a connection string; SSL, character set, retries and dates are set for you.

1.title: Options win
1.text: Options always override the connection string.

3.title: Full Unicode
3.text: `utf8mb4` stores Persian text and emoji correctly.

1.title: Security settings
1.text:
`AddOSMySql` registers your context through the core. The options always win over the connection string: `SslMode` is `Required` (`VerifyFull` with `VerifyServerCertificate`, `Preferred` only when you set `Encrypt = false`).

`AllowPublicKeyRetrieval` is off, because fetching the server's key over an unchecked connection invites a man-in-the-middle.

2.title: Characters and collation
2.text: `CharacterSet` is `utf8mb4`, so Persian text and emoji are stored correctly. Set a collation in your model with `modelBuilder.UseCollation(...)` if you need one.

3.title: Retry and dates
3.text:
With `RetryOnFailure` on, the provider's own retrying strategy is used with `RetryCount` and `RetryDelay` from `EFCoreOptions`.

Every `DateTimeOffset` is stored as UTC `datetime(6)`; the provider's default `datetime` would drop fractional seconds.

4.title: Strict mode and migrations
4.text:
Keep MySQL's strict mode (`STRICT_TRANS_TABLES`, on by default in MySQL 8): it makes a too-long value fail with `data.tooLong` instead of being cut silently.

MySQL has no schemas, so for migrations only `HistoryTable` matters.

secure.title: What the connection really uses
secure.note: The string asked for no SSL, public key retrieval and latin1; the options overrode all three.

collation.title: Choose a collation
collation.note: Collation is part of the model, so it lives in `OnModelCreating`, not in the connection.

type.MySqlOptions: The connection string, character set and the security and retry switches.

MySqlOptions.VerifyServerCertificate: Also checks the server's certificate and host name (`VerifyFull`). Off by default; turn it on when the server has a proper certificate.
MySqlOptions.CharacterSet: The connection character set. `utf8mb4` by default; must not be empty.

MySqlEx.AddOSMySql: Registers a context on MySQL. Registers OS.EFCore too when it is not registered yet, so one call is enough; call `AddOSEFCore` as well, before or after, only to change its settings.
MySqlEx.UseOSMySql: Applies the MySQL setup to a builder.

errors.title: Errors and what was tested
errors.summary: How MySQL errors turn into results, and an honest note on testing.

1.title: Known numbers
1.text: Common MySQL error numbers map to stable `data.*` codes.

2.title: Wrong password
2.text: A wrong user or password is `data.error` on purpose.

4.title: Honest note
4.text: Only unit tests so far; no real MySQL server yet.

1.title: Recognized numbers
1.text:
These MySQL error numbers are recognized (checked against the official MySQL reference): 1062 gives `data.duplicate` with the index, 1048 gives `data.required` with the column, 1452 gives `data.missingRef`, 1451 gives `data.inUse`, 1406 and 1264 give `data.tooLong`.

1213 (deadlock) and 1205 (lock wait timeout) give `data.busy`, and 1040, 1042, 2002, 2003, 2006 and 2013 give `data.offline`.

2.title: Wrong password
2.text: A wrong user or password (1045) is `data.error` on purpose: it is not temporary, it is not retried, and its message, which contains the user and host, never reaches a result. Anything else is `data.error`.

3.title: Honest note
3.text:
This package has been tested only with unit tests (the error table, the connection settings, the retry strategy, the model and the date storage).

It has not yet run against a real MySQL server; do that before you rely on it in production.

save-item.title: Turn a MySQL result into a message
save-item.note: An out-of-range number (1264) also arrives as `data.tooLong`.

provider.title: Provider and license
provider.summary: Which MySQL provider runs today, under which license, and why your code does not care.

1.title: Oracle provider
1.text: Today the package runs on Oracle's `MySql.EntityFrameworkCore`.

2.title: Why
2.text: Pomelo (MIT) has no stable release for EF Core 10 yet.

3.title: License
3.text: Oracle's packages are GPL-2.0-only with the Universal FOSS Exception.

4.title: Easy move
4.text: Your code stays as it is when the package moves to Pomelo.

1.title: Which provider and why
1.text: Today the package runs on Oracle's `MySql.EntityFrameworkCore`, because the open-source alternative, Pomelo (MIT license), has no stable release for EF Core 10 yet.

2.title: License and limits
2.text:
Oracle's packages are licensed GPL-2.0-only with the Universal FOSS Exception; check this against how you distribute your app before you ship.

Oracle's provider supports MySQL only, not MariaDB.

3.title: Moving later
3.text: Because `AddOSMySql` and `MySqlOptions` expose no provider type, the package can move to Pomelo when it ships for EF Core 10, which also brings MariaDB, and your code stays as it is.

from-settings.title: Your code only knows our API
from-settings.note: No Oracle or Pomelo type appears here, so a provider switch changes nothing in this code.
